samples_reviewed.question_text: The distance from the bench to the tree is 2 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 1 m. Which distance is longer in meters?
How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.
A pencil is 10 cm long. A ruler is 15 cm long. Which length is shorter in cm?
A notebook is 20 cm long. A pencil is 10 cm long. Which length is shorter in cm?
How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.
A pencil is 10 cm long. A notebook is 20 cm long. Which length is longer in cm?
A spoon is 20 cm long. A pencil is 19 cm long. Which length is shorter in cm?
The distance from the bench to the tree is 82 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 37 m. Which distance is longer in meters?
The distance from the bench to the tree is 65 m. The distance from the gate to the tree is 47 m. Which distance is shorter in meters?
A notebook is 20 cm long. A spoon is 12 cm long. Which length is longer in cm?
A school fence is 10 m long. A garden path is 9 m long. Which length is longer in m?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Measuring and comparing are both represented, with the stem How long is the object? Give your answer in cm. covering the tool-reading side. The comparison items are undercut by their option sets: the bench-and-tree stem naming 2 m and 1 m offers 3 and 7 as choices, values that appear nowhere in the problem and that no reading of the situation could produce.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both directions of comparison are generated, longer and shorter, and all three units named by the competency are exercised: object length in centimetres, object length in metres via the fence and path item, and distance between locations in metres. Direct measurement from a rendered object also appears.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Two short declarative sentences followed by a question is the standard frame here, and the objects chosen, pencil, notebook, spoon, ruler, are all familiar classroom items. The comparison demands no computation, only reading two quantities, which suits Grade 2 Quarter 2.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three response types appear, including a rendered measuring item, and the contexts split cleanly between object-to-object comparison and location-to-location distance. That spread covers the presentational range the competency implies without padding.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty across seeds moves by magnitude alone, from a 2 m versus 1 m pairing up to 82 m versus 37 m, but the cognitive task never changes: pick the larger or smaller of two printed numerals. Using an appropriate measuring tool, the clause that distinguishes this competency from plain number comparison, is reached by only two seeds.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Centimetre lengths sit between roughly 10 and 20, which matches real pencils and notebooks, and metre distances top out in the eighties, a believable schoolyard span. Nothing strays into ranges a Grade 2 learner could not picture or add.
